title.zh: 卷29 列傳第21 王傑 王勇 宇文虯 宇文盛 弟丘 耿豪 高琳 李和 伊婁穆 楊紹 王雅 達奚寔 劉雄 侯植
title.en: Volume 29 Biographies 21: Wang Jie; Wang Yong; Yu Wenqiu; Yu Wencheng; younger brother Qiu; Geng Hao; Gao Lin; Li He; Yi Loumu; Yang Shao; Wang Ya; Da Xishi; Liu Xiong; Hou Zhi
title.raw: 卷29 列傳第21 王傑 王勇 宇文虯 宇文盛 弟丘 耿豪 高琳 李和 伊婁穆 楊紹 王雅 達奚寔 劉雄 侯植 Volume 29 Biographies 21: Wang Jie; Wang Yong; Yu Wenqiu; Yu Wencheng; younger brother Qiu; Geng Hao; Gao Lin; Li He; Yi Loumu; Yang Shao; Wang Ya; Da Xishi; Liu Xiong; Hou Zhi

sentences.zh: 王傑，金城直城人也，本名文達。

translations.literal: Wang Jie was a native of Zhicheng in Jincheng; his original name was Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie came from Zhicheng in Jincheng; he had originally been called Wenda.

sentences.zh: 高祖萬國，魏伏波將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wanguo was Wei's General Who Quells the Waves and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wanguo had served Wei as General Who Quells the Waves and inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 父巢，龍驤將軍、榆中鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Chao was General of the Flying Dragon and garrison commander of Yuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao held the titles General of the Flying Dragon and commander of the Yuzhong garrison.

sentences.zh: 傑少有壯志，每以功名自許。

translations.literal: Jie in youth had lofty ambition and always pledged himself to achievement and fame.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jie burned with ambition, always measuring himself against great deeds and lasting renown.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，有膂力。

translations.literal: He was skilled in mounted archery and possessed bodily strength.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at horseback archery and had uncommon physical strength.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，起家子都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign, he entered service as a junior area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei came to the throne, he began his career as a junior commander.

sentences.zh: 後從西遷，賜爵都昌縣子。

translations.literal: Later he followed the westward migration and was granted the title Viscount of Duchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the court's flight to the west and was ennobled as Viscount of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 太祖奇其才，擢授揚烈將軍、羽林監，尋加都督。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor marveled at his talent, promoted him to General Who Raises Might and Commandant of the Forest of Feathers, and soon added the title Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, struck by his gifts, raised him to General Who Raises Might and commandant of the Feathered Guard, then shortly made him an area commander as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂諸將曰：「王文達萬人敵也，但恐勇決太過耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once told the generals: "Wang Wenda is a match for ten thousand men, but I only fear his bold decisiveness goes too far.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told his commanders, "Wang Wenda could stand against ten thousand — I only worry that his courage cuts too deep and leaves no room for caution.

sentences.zh: 」復潼關，破沙苑，爭河橋，戰邙山，皆以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: " At the recovery of Tong Pass, the break at Shaye, the struggle at Heqiao, and the battle at Mount Mang, he was everywhere known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, Shaye, Heqiao, and Mount Mang he fought with such daring that his name became synonymous with courage on the front.

sentences.zh: 親待日隆，賞賜加於倫等。

translations.literal: Day by day personal favor grew, and rewards exceeded those of his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor toward him deepened daily, and his gifts outstripped those of men his equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 於是賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 除岐州刺史，加撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，進爵為公，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Qi Province, additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grandee of the Silver Seal with Blue Ribbon, advanced in rank to duke with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Qi, given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Silver Seal Grandee, and promoted to duke with eight hundred feudal households.

sentences.zh: 累遷大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Grand Area Commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and Grand Master with the Grand Prefecture equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through grand area commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, palace attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and grand master with a grand prefecture matching the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，從于謹圍江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he followed Yu Jin in besieging Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he marched under Yu Jin to besiege Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時柵內有人善用長矟，戰士將登者，多為所斃。

translations.literal: At that time within the palisade there was a man skilled with the long spear; of warriors about to scale the wall, many were killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palisade stood a man who wielded a long spear with deadly skill; warriors who tried to climb the works fell to him in swarms.

sentences.zh: 謹令傑射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Jin ordered Jie to shoot him; at the release of the string he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ordered Jie to bring him down, and one shaft laid him out.

sentences.zh: 登者乃得入，餘衆繼進，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Those scaling could then enter; the rest of the force followed in, and they took the place.
translations.idiomatic: With the spearman dead, the climbers poured over the wall; the main body followed and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 謹喜曰：「濟我大事者，在公此箭也。

translations.literal: Jin said with pleasure: "He who completed my great affair is this arrow of yours.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said warmly, "This single arrow of yours decided the whole campaign for me.
End of quotation.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵張掖郡公，增邑一千戶，出為河州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Jie was advanced to Duke of Zhangye commandery with an additional fief of one thousand households and sent out as Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, Jie was made Duke of Zhangye with one thousand additional households and posted as inspector of He.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以傑勳望俱重，故授以本州。

translations.literal: The court, because Jie's merit and standing were both weighty, therefore appointed him to his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jie's battlefield record and reputation both commanded respect, the court gave him his home province.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he rose to grand general.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔傑與隨公楊忠自

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered Jie and Duke of Sui Yang Zhong from
translations.idiomatic: That same year an edict sent Jie and Duke of Sui Yang Zhong north from the frontier

translations.literal: (Han) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Han]

sentences.zh: 〔漠〕北伐齊，至幷州而還。

translations.literal: 〔desert/steppe〕 [emended: Han] to campaign north against Qi, reaching Bing Province and returning.
translations.idiomatic: across the northern steppe to campaign against Qi, reaching Bing Province before turning back.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，除宜州刺史，增邑通前三千六百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was appointed Inspector of Yi Province, with fief increased in all to three thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he became inspector of Yi, his total fief rising to three thousand six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 六年，從齊公憲東禦齊將斛律明月，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he followed Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian east to repel Qi general Hulu Mingyue and was promoted to Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched east under Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian against the Qi general Hulu Mingyue and was made a pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 建德初，除涇州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Grand Commander of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande opened he was made grand commander of Jing.

sentences.zh: 傑少從軍旅，雖不習吏事，所歷州府，咸以忠恕為心，以是頗為百姓所慕。

translations.literal: Jie from youth followed the army; though he did not study civil administration, in every province and prefecture he served he took loyalty and forbearance as his heart, and for this the common people greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had soldiered since youth and never mastered civil office, yet in every post he governed with loyalty and mercy, and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jie was appointed Upper Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Jie was made upper pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，薨，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Daxiang, at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈河鄯鄧延洮宕翼七州諸軍事、河州刺史，追封鄂國公。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded command over military affairs in the seven provinces of He, Shan, Deng, Yan, Tao, Dang, and Yi, and the post of Inspector of He Province; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of E state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with command over He, Shan, Deng, Yan, Tao, Dang, and Yi and the post of inspector of He, and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of E.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子孝僊，大象末，位至開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoxian, at the end of Daxiang, reached the rank of Grand Master with the Grand Prefecture equal to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoxian, by the end of Daxiang, had risen to grand master with a grand prefecture matching the grand general.

sentences.zh: 王勇，代武川人也，本名胡仁。

translations.literal: Wang Yong was a native of Wuchuan in Dai; his original name was Huren.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong came from Wuchuan in Dai; he had originally been called Huren.

sentences.zh: 少雄健，有膽決，便弓馬，膂力過人。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and hardy, had daring and decision, was adept with bow and horse, and his bodily strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was fierce and resolute, skilled with bow and saddle, and stronger than ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，万俟醜奴等寇亂關隴，勇占募隨軍討之，以功授甯朔將軍、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era of Wei, Wan Sitou Chounu and others raided and ravaged Guan and Long; Yong recruited followers and joined the army in suppressing them, and for merit was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yong'an era, when Wan Sitou Chounu and others ravaged Guan and Long, Yong raised troops and campaigned against them, earning the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 又數從侯莫陳悅、賀拔岳征討，功每居多，拜別將。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly followed Hou Mochen Yue and He Ba Yue on punitive campaigns; his achievement each time ranked foremost, and he was appointed Separate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again and again under Hou Mochen Yue and He Ba Yue, usually leading in merit, until he was made a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 及太祖為丞相，引為帳內直蕩都督，加後將軍、太中大夫，封包信縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became chancellor, he brought Yong in as direct-charge area commander within the command tent, additionally made Rear General and Grand Master of the Palace, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Baoxin County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became chancellor, he took Yong into his personal staff as direct-charge area commander, made him rear general and palace grand master, and enfeoffed him Viscount of Baoxin with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，增邑四百戶，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, his fief was increased by four hundred households and his rank advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong his fief grew by four hundred households and he was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，氣蓋衆軍，所當必破。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle at Shaye, his spirit overawed the whole army; wherever he faced the enemy he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle of Shaye his presence dominated the field; every line he struck gave way.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎其勇敢，賞賜特隆。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed at his bravery and rewarded him with exceptional largesse.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marveled at his courage and heaped rewards on him beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，邑一千五百戶，拜鎮南將軍，授帥都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to duke with a fief of one thousand five hundred households, appointed General Who Guards the South, and given the post of army area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to duke with fifteen hundred households, made General Who Guards the South, and given command of an army district.

sentences.zh: 從討趙青雀，平之，論功居最，除衛大將軍、殷州刺史，加通直散騎常侍，兼太子武衛率。

translations.literal: Following the suppression of Zhao Qingque and his pacification, in reckoning merit he ranked first; he was appointed Guard Grand General and Inspector of Yin Province, additionally made Regular Attendant of Direct Dispatches and Scattered Cavalry, and concurrently Crown Prince Martial Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Zhao Qingque, his merit stood first; he was made guard grand general and inspector of Yin, given the added posts of regular attendant of direct dispatches and scattered cavalry, and made crown prince martial guard commander as well.

sentences.zh: 邙山之戰，勇率敢死之士三百人，並執短兵，大呼直進，出入衝擊，殺傷甚多，敵人無敢當者。

translations.literal: In the battle at Mount Mang, Yong led three hundred death-defying men, all bearing short weapons; shouting, they drove straight forward, charging in and out, killing and wounding many, and none of the enemy dared stand against them.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang Yong led three hundred men sworn to die, all with short blades; shouting, they drove straight through the enemy lines, killing many, and no foe dared meet them.

sentences.zh: 是役也，大軍不利，唯勇及王文達、耿令貴三人力戰，皆有殊功。

translations.literal: In that battle the great army fared ill; only Yong, Wang Wenda, and Geng Linggui fought with all their strength, each winning extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: That day the main force faltered; only Yong, Wang Wenda, and Geng Linggui fought on with desperate valor, each earning extraordinary distinction.

sentences.zh: 太祖於是賞帛二千疋，令自分之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon rewarded them with two thousand bolts of silk and ordered them to divide it among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then gave them two thousand bolts of silk and told them to divide the reward themselves.

sentences.zh: 軍還，皆拜上州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, all three were appointed inspectors of upper provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On their return all three were made inspectors of first-rank provinces.

sentences.zh: 以雍州、岐州、北雍州擬授勇等，然州頗有優劣，又令探籌取之。

translations.literal: Yong Province, Qi Province, and Northern Yong Province were intended for Yong and the others, but the provinces differed greatly in quality, so they were told to draw lots from a jar to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, Qi, and Northern Yong were set aside for them, but the provinces were not equal in value, so lots were drawn from a jar.

sentences.zh: 勇遂得雍州，文達得岐州，令貴得北雍州。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon obtained Yong Province, Wenda obtained Qi Province, and Linggui obtained Northern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yong drew Yong, Wenda drew Qi, and Linggui drew Northern Yong.

sentences.zh: 仍賜勇名為勇，令貴名豪，文達名傑，以彰其功。

translations.literal: They were further granted names to mark their achievement: Yong was given the name Yong, Linggui the name Hao, and Wenda the name Jie.
translations.idiomatic: To honor their deeds they were also given new names: Yong received the name Yong, Linggui the name Hao, and Wenda the name Jie.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授大都督，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Area Commander and transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became grand area commander, then bearer of the staff of authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and Grand Master with the Grand Prefecture equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he rose to palace attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and grand master with a grand prefecture matching the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，從柱國趙貴征茹茹，破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he followed Pillar-of-State Zhao Gui in campaigning against the Ruru and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he marched under Pillar-of-State Zhao Gui against the Ruru and broke them.

sentences.zh: 勇追擊，獲雜畜數千頭。

translations.literal: Yong pursued the attack and captured several thousand head of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pursued and seized several thousand head of mixed herds.

sentences.zh: 進爵新陽郡公，增邑通前二千戶，仍賜姓庫汗氏。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Xinyang commandery, with fief increased in all to two thousand households, and further granted the surname of the Kuhon clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Xinyang with a total fief of two thousand households and granted the surname of the Kuhon clan.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜稍伯中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Shaobo Middle Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made shaobo middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 又論討茹茹功，別封永固縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Again, in reckoning merit from the campaign against the Ruru, he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yonggu County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Merit against the Ruru brought a separate enfeoffment as Baron of Yonggu with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時有別封者，例聽回授次子，勇獨請封兄子元興，時人義之。

translations.literal: At that time those with separate enfeoffments were by precedent allowed to transfer the title to a second son; Yong alone asked that his elder brother's son Yuanxing be enfeoffed, and men of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Separate enfeoffments were usually passed to a second son, but Yong alone asked that his brother's son Yuanxing receive the title, and contemporaries honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，岷山羌豪鞏廉俱和叛，勇帥師討平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, the Minshan Qiang chieftain Gong Lianjuhe rebelled; Yong led troops to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign the Minshan Qiang chieftain Gong Lianjuhe rebelled; Yong led an army and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 勇性雄猛，為當時驍將。

translations.literal: Yong by nature was bold and fierce and was a fierce general of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was by nature fierce and ranked among the boldest commanders of his day.

sentences.zh: 然矜功伐善，好揚人之惡，時論亦以此鄙之。

translations.literal: Yet he prided himself on merit and disparaged others' goodness, loved to broadcast men's faults, and contemporary opinion also despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he boasted of his deeds, belittled others' virtues, and loved to broadcast their faults; public opinion scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 柱國侯莫陳崇，勳高望重，與諸將同謁晉公護，聞勇數論人之短，乃於衆中折辱之。

translations.literal: Pillar-of-State Hou Mochen Chong, whose merit was high and standing weighty, together with the other generals paid a call on Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu; hearing that Yong often discussed others' shortcomings, he thereupon humiliated him before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-of-State Hou Mochen Chong, a man of high merit and greater standing, was visiting Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu with the other commanders when he heard Yong traducing others again and publicly shamed him before them all.

sentences.zh: 勇遂慙恚，因疽發背而卒。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon felt shame and rage, and because of a carbuncle on his back he died.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified and enraged, Yong fell ill with an abscess on his back and died.

sentences.zh: 子昌嗣，官至大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Changsi reached the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changsi rose to grand general.

sentences.zh: 宇文虯

translations.literal: Yuwen Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Qiu (虯)

sentences.zh: 宇文虯字樂仁，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Qiu, styled Leren, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Qiu, styled Leren, came from Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 性驍悍，有膽略。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and bold, with daring and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce by nature, bold in counsel and resolute in action.

sentences.zh: 少從軍征討，累有戰功。

translations.literal: From youth he followed the army on punitive campaigns and repeatedly had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he campaigned with the army and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，除征虜將軍、中散大夫，加都督。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era of Wei he was appointed General Who Captures the Barbarians and Palace Scattered Grandee, with the added title Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yong'an era he was made General Who Captures the Barbarians and palace scattered grandee, with the added rank of area commander.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，從獨孤信在荊州，破梁人於下溠，遂平歐陽、酇城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign, he followed Dugu Xin in Jing Province, defeated Liang forces at Xiazhi, and thereupon pacified Ouyang and Zuo city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei came to the throne, Qiu followed Dugu Xin in Jing, routed the Liang at Xiazhi, and then took Ouyang and Zuo city.

sentences.zh: 虯俘獲甚多。

translations.literal: Qiu captured prisoners in great number.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu took a great many captives.

sentences.zh: 又攻南陽、廣平二城，擒郡守一人。

translations.literal: He also attacked the two cities of Nanyang and Guangping and captured one prefectural administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He also stormed Nanyang and Guangping and captured a prefectural administrator.

sentences.zh: 以功加安西將軍、銀青光祿大夫、員外、直閤將軍、閤內都督，封南安縣侯，邑九百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the West, Grandee of the Silver Seal with Blue Ribbon, Outside-the-Register Attendant, Direct Palace General, and Inner-Palace Area Commander, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an County with a fief of nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received the added titles General Who Pacifies the West, Silver Seal Grandee, outside attendant, direct palace general, and inner-palace area commander, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Nan'an with nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，以獨孤信為行臺，信引虯為帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu moved west, Dugu Xin was made mobile headquarters commissioner, and Xin brought Qiu in as area commander within the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Dugu Xin became mobile headquarters commissioner and took Qiu into his personal staff as tent area commander.

sentences.zh: 破田八能及擒東魏荊州刺史辛纂，虯功居多。

translations.literal: In defeating Tian Baneng and capturing Eastern Wei's Inspector of Jing Province Xin Zuan, Qiu's achievement ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the defeat of Tian Baneng and capture of Eastern Wei's Jing inspector Xin Zuan, Qiu's merit stood first.

sentences.zh: 尋隨信奔梁。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Xin in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Xin into exile in Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，歸闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year three he came back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷論前後功，增邑四百戶，進爵為公。

translations.literal: The court reckoned his earlier and later merit, increased his fief by four hundred households, and advanced his rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: The court reviewed his service before and after, added four hundred households to his fief, and promoted him to duke.

sentences.zh: 擒竇泰，復弘農，及沙苑、河橋之戰，皆有功。

translations.literal: In capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and the battles at Shaye and Heqiao, he had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battles of Shaye and Heqiao, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 增邑八百戶，進車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by eight hundred households, and he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred households were added to his fief, and he rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.

sentences.zh: 七年，除漢陽郡守，又從獨孤信討梁仚定，破之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Administrator of Hanyang commandery, and again followed Dugu Xin in suppressing Liang's Xian Ding and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became administrator of Hanyang, then followed Dugu Xin against Liang's Xian Ding and broke him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出為南秦州刺史，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was sent out as Inspector of Southern Qin Province, additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and promoted to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and Grand Master with the Grand Prefecture equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was posted as inspector of Southern Qin, given General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, then promoted to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and grand master with a grand prefecture matching the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 追論斬辛纂功，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In retrospective reckoning of merit for beheading Xin Zuan, his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Merit for slaying Xin Zuan brought one thousand additional households.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與大將軍王雄征上津、魏興等，竝平之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, together with Grand General Wang Xiong, he campaigned against Shangjin, Weixing, and others, and together pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he joined Grand General Wang Xiong in campaigns against Shangjin, Weixing, and other posts, and together they pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 又于白馬與武陵王蕭紀將楊乾運戰，破之。

translations.literal: Again at Baima he fought Liang Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji's general Yang Qianyun and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At Baima he also fought Yang Qianyun, general to Liang's Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 虯每經行陣，必身先卒伍，故上下同心，戰無不克。

translations.literal: Whenever Qiu passed through the battle line, he always placed himself ahead of the rank and file; therefore above and below were of one mind, and in battle there was none he did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qiu entered the line he led from the front; officers and men fought as one, and he never failed to win.

sentences.zh: 尋而魏興復叛，虯又與王雄討平之。

translations.literal: Soon Weixing rebelled again; Qiu again joined Wang Xiong in suppressing and pacifying it.
translations.idiomatic: When Weixing rebelled again, Qiu and Wang Xiong crushed the revolt once more.

sentences.zh: 俄除金州刺史，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Inspector of Jin Province and promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made inspector of Jin and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward of disease.

sentences.zh: 宇文盛

translations.literal: Yuwen Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Sheng (盛)

sentences.zh: 宇文盛字保興，代人也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Sheng, styled Baoxing, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Sheng, styled Baoxing, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖伊與敦、祖長壽、父文孤，並為沃野鎮軍主。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yiyudun, grandfather Changshou, and father Wengu all served as garrison commanders of Woye.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yiyudun, grandfather Changshou, and father Wengu had all been garrison commanders at Woye.

sentences.zh: 盛志力驍雄。

translations.literal: Sheng's will and strength were fierce and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was fierce in spirit and formidable in strength.

sentences.zh: 初為太祖帳內，從破侯莫陳悅，授威烈將軍，封漁陽縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At first he served within the Grand Progenitor's command tent; following the defeat of Hou Mochen Yue, he was appointed General of Majestic Might and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yuyang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He began in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's personal staff; after the defeat of Hou Mochen Yue he was made General of Majestic Might and enfeoffed Viscount of Yuyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，兼都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he was additionally made Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he was also made area commander.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，授都督、平遠將軍、步兵校尉，進爵為公，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the break at Shaye, he was appointed Area Commander, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Colonel of the Foot Soldiers, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle of Shaye he was made area commander, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and colonel of the foot soldiers, promoted to duke, and given eight hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 除馮翊郡守，加帥都督、西安州大中正、通直散騎常侍、撫軍將軍，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Fufeng commandery, additionally made Army Area Commander, Senior Rectifier of Western An Province, Regular Attendant of Direct Dispatches and Scattered Cavalry, and General Who Pacifies the Army, with fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Fufeng, given the added posts of army area commander, senior rectifier of Western An, regular attendant of direct dispatches and scattered cavalry, and General Who Pacifies the Army, with three hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 累遷大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he rose to area commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three-Duke honors, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through area commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three-Duke honors, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Palace with Three-Duke rank, to inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 及楚公趙貴謀為亂，盛密赴京告之。

translations.literal: When Duke of Chu Zhao Gui plotted rebellion, Sheng secretly went to the capital to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Chu Zhao Gui plotted rebellion, Sheng secretly went to the capital to report him.

sentences.zh: 貴誅，授大將軍，進爵忠城郡公，除涇州都督，賜甲一領、奴婢二百口、馬五百疋，牛羊及莊田、什物等稱是。

translations.literal: When Gui was executed, Sheng was appointed Grand General, advanced to Duke of Zhongcheng commandery, made Area Commander of Jing Province, and granted one suit of armor, two hundred slaves, five hundred horses, cattle and sheep, estates and fields, and goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Gui was executed, Sheng was made grand general and Duke of Zhongcheng, appointed area commander of Jing, and given armor, two hundred slaves, five hundred horses, livestock, estates, and goods in proportion.

sentences.zh: 仍從賀蘭祥平洮陽

translations.literal: He still followed Helan Xiang in pacifying Taoyang
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned under Helan Xiang to pacify Taoyang

translations.literal: (Gong) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Gong]

sentences.zh: 〔洪〕和二城，別封一子甘棠縣公。

translations.literal: 〔Hong〕 [emended: Gong] and the two cities; a son was separately enfeoffed Duke of Gantang County.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the two cities; one son was separately enfeoffed Duke of Gantang County.

sentences.zh: 轉延州總管，進位柱國。

translations.literal: Transferred to overall commander of Yan Province; advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall commander of Yan Province and advanced to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 丘字胡奴，起家襄威將軍、奉朝請、都督，賜爵臨邑縣子。

translations.literal: Qiu styled Hunu; he began his career as General of Majestic Might, Attendant at Court, and area commander, and was granted noble rank as Baron of Linyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu, styled Hunu, entered service as General of Majestic Might, attendant at court, and area commander, and was enfeoffed Baron of Linyi County.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State and grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Assists the State and grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 預告趙貴謀，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵安義縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: For forewarning Zhao Gui's plot, he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Three-Duke honors, advanced to Marquis of Anyi County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For warning of Zhao Gui's plot he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with Three-Duke honors and Marquis of Anyi County with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公，除咸陽郡守。

translations.literal: He was further given Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, advanced to duke, and made Administrator of Xianyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and grand master of the palace with Three-Duke rank, raised to duke, and appointed administrator of Xianyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inspector of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 入為左宮伯，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Left Palace Baron and advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as left palace baron and was advanced to grand general.

sentences.zh: 出為延綏丹三州三防諸軍事、延州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as overseer of military affairs for Yan, Sui, and Dan provinces and the three garrisons, and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to oversee military affairs in Yan, Sui, and Dan provinces and the three garrisons, and made inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 轉涼甘瓜三州諸軍事、涼州刺史，加柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: Transferred to overseer of military affairs for Liang, Gan, and Gua provinces and Inspector of Liang Province; given the title Grand General and Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command military affairs in Liang, Gan, and Gua provinces and made inspector of Liang, with the title grand general and pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 建德元年薨，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jiande, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國、宜鄜等州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded pillar-of-state and Inspector of Yi, Mei, and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as pillar-of-state and inspector of Yi, Mei, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 子隴嗣。

translations.literal: His son Long succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Long succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 耿豪，鉅鹿人也。

translations.literal: Geng Hao was a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Hao came from Julu.

sentences.zh: 本名令貴。

translations.literal: His original name was Linggui.
translations.idiomatic: He had been born Linggui.

sentences.zh: 其先避劉、石之亂，居遼東，因仕於燕。

translations.literal: His forebears, fleeing the chaos of the Liu and Shi regimes, dwelt in Liaodong and thereupon served Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears fled the chaos of the Liu and Shi regimes to Liaodong and entered the service of Yan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖超，率衆歸魏，遂家於神武川。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chao led the multitude in submitting to Wei and thereupon made his home at Shenwu River.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chao led his followers in submitting to Wei and settled the family at Shenwu River.

sentences.zh: 豪少麄獷，有武藝，好以氣淩人。

translations.literal: Hao in youth was rough and fierce, had martial skill, and liked to overbear others by force of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Young Hao was rough and fierce, skilled in arms, and prone to browbeat others.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳西征，引為帳內。

translations.literal: When He Ba Yue campaigned west, he brought Hao into his personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ba Yue marched west, he took Hao into his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 岳被害，歸太祖，以武勇見知。

translations.literal: When Yue was murdered, Hao returned to the Grand Progenitor and, through martial valor, won recognition.
translations.idiomatic: After He Ba Yue was murdered, Hao entered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's service and won notice for martial valor.

sentences.zh: 豪亦自謂所事得主。

translations.literal: Hao also considered that the lord he served was the right master.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also felt he had found the right master.

sentences.zh: 從討侯莫陳悅及迎魏孝武，錄前後功，封平原縣子，邑三百戶，除寧朔將軍、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: Following the punitive campaign against Houmochen Yue and the welcome of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, his earlier and later merits were recorded; he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyuan County with a fief of three hundred households, and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Houmochen Yue and escorting Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west, he was rewarded for his service with Baron of Pingyuan County and three hundred households, General Who Pacifies the North, and commandant of the imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍，加通直散騎常侍，進爵為侯，增邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Promoted to General Who Captures Foes, given Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access, advanced to marquis, fief increased by seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Captures Foes and regular attendant of unimpeded access, raised to marquis, and given seven hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，豪先鋒陷陣，加前將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai and the recovery of Hongnong, Hao as vanguard broke the enemy ranks; he was given the title Forward General and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Dou Tai and the recovery of Hongnong, Hao led the vanguard through the enemy lines and was made forward general and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之戰，豪殺傷甚多，血染甲裳盡赤。

translations.literal: In the battle of Shaye, Hao killed and wounded many; blood soaked his armor and robes until they were wholly red.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaye, Hao killed and wounded many; blood soaked his armor and robes until they were wholly red.

sentences.zh: 太祖見之，歎曰：「令貴武猛，所向無前，觀其甲裳，足以為驗，不須更論級數也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw it and sighed, saying: "Linggui is fierce in battle; wherever he turns there is none before him. Look at his armor and robes—that is proof enough; there is no need to discuss rank by grades.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw it and sighed, "Linggui fights with brutal force and nothing stands before him. His blood-soaked armor is proof enough—no need to quibble over grades of merit.

sentences.zh: 」於是進爵為公，增邑通前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was advanced to duke; fief increased to one thousand five hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon raised Hao to duke and increased his fief to one thousand five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 除鎮北將軍、金紫光祿大夫、南郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn, and Inspector of South Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the North, golden grandee of the purple dawn, and inspector of South Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 九年，從太祖戰於邙山，豪謂所部曰：「大丈夫見賊，須右手拔刀，左手把矛，直刺直斫，慎莫皺眉畏死。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, following the Grand Progenitor in battle at Mount Mang, Hao told his troops: "When a great man meets the enemy, he must draw his sword with the right hand and grasp his spear with the left, thrusting and hacking straight on—take care not to knit your brows in fear of death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, fighting with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai at Mount Mang, Hao told his men, "A true man meeting the enemy draws his sword with his right hand and his spear with his left, thrusting and hacking straight on—never shrink from death.

sentences.zh: 」遂大呼獨入，敵人鋒刃亂下，當時咸謂豪歿。

translations.literal: " He then shouted and charged in alone; enemy blades rained down, and those who stood before Hao fell wounded or dead in succession.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he shouted and charged in alone; enemy blades rained down, and every man who stood before him fell wounded or dead.

sentences.zh: 俄然奮刀而還。

translations.literal: Presently he flourished his blade and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he flourished his blade and fought his way back.

sentences.zh: 戰數合，當豪前者，死傷相繼。

translations.literal: After several clashes, those who faced Hao were wounded or killed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After several clashes, whoever faced Hao was wounded or killed in turn.

sentences.zh: 又謂左右曰：「吾豈樂殺人，但壯士除賊，不得不爾。

translations.literal: He again told those beside him: "Do I delight in killing men? But a stalwart removing bandits cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "Do I delight in killing? A fighting man clearing out bandits cannot do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 若不能殺賊，又不為人所傷，何異逐坐人也。

translations.literal: If one cannot kill bandits and is not wounded by others either, what difference is there from chasing seated men?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot kill the enemy and are not wounded either, you might as well be chasing men who sit still.

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘉之，拜北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor praised him and appointed him Inspector of North Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him and made him inspector of North Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 十三年，論前後戰功，進授車騎大將軍、儀同三司，增邑通前一千八百戶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, reviewing earlier and later battle merit, he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Three-Duke honors; fief increased to one thousand eight hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his battle merits were reviewed and he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with Three-Duke honors; his fief reached one thousand eight hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 十五年，賜姓和稽氏，進位侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was granted the surname Heji, and advanced to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was granted the surname Heji and advanced to attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of agile cavalry, and grand master of the palace with Three-Duke rank.

sentences.zh: 豪性凶悍，言多不遜。

translations.literal: Hao by nature was fierce and brutal; his words were often insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was fierce by nature and often spoke insolently.

sentences.zh: 太祖惜其驍勇，每優容之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor valued his martial dash and always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai valued his fighting spirit and always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 豪亦自謂意氣冠群，終無所屈。

translations.literal: Hao also considered his spirit and force to surpass the group, and in the end never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also believed his spirit outmatched everyone else and would never bow to another.

sentences.zh: 李穆、蔡佑初與豪同時開府，後竝居豪之右。

translations.literal: Li Mu and Cai You at first opened grand masterships together with Hao; later both ranked above Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu and Cai You had opened grand masterships together with Hao, but later both ranked above him.

sentences.zh: 豪意不平，謂太祖曰：「外聞物議，謂豪勝李穆、蔡佑。

translations.literal: Hao resented this and said to the Grand Progenitor: "Outside one hears public talk saying Hao surpasses Li Mu and Cai You.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful, Hao told Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, "People outside say I surpass Li Mu and Cai You.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "How do you say that?
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Progenitor asked, "How so?

sentences.zh: 」豪曰：「世言李穆、蔡佑，丞相臂膊；

translations.literal: " Hao said: "The world says Li Mu and Cai You are the chancellor's arms and forearms;
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "People say Li Mu and Cai You are the chancellor's arms and forearms;

sentences.zh: 耿豪、王勇，丞相咽項。

translations.literal: Geng Hao and Wang Yong are the chancellor's throat and nape.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Hao and Wang Yong guard the chancellor like throat and nape.

sentences.zh: 以咽項在上，故為勝也。

translations.literal: Since throat and nape are above, therefore they are superior.
translations.idiomatic: The throat and nape are above, so we are superior.

sentences.zh: 」豪之麄猛，皆此類。

translations.literal: " Hao's roughness and fierceness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao's roughness and bravado were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: 太祖痛惜之，贈以本官，加朔州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor grieved for him and posthumously awarded his former offices, adding Inspector of Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai grieved for him, posthumously confirmed his offices, and added inspector of Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 子雄嗣，位至大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiong succeeded, reaching the rank of grand general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong succeeded him and rose to grand general.

sentences.zh: 高琳字季珉，其先高句麗人也。

translations.literal: Gao Lin, styled Jimin, his forebears were men of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lin, styled Jimin, came from Goguryeo stock.

sentences.zh: 六世祖欽，為質於慕容廆，遂仕於燕。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Qin was sent as hostage to Murong Hui and thereupon served Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Qin was sent as a hostage to Murong Hui and entered Yan's service.

sentences.zh: 五世祖宗，率衆歸魏，拜第一領民酋長，賜姓羽真氏。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zong led the multitude in submitting to Wei, was appointed First Chief of Settled Peoples, and granted the surname Yuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Zong led his followers in submitting to Wei, was made first chief of settled peoples, and granted the surname Yuzhen.

sentences.zh: 祖明、父遷仕魏，咸亦顯達。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ming and father Qian served Wei; both likewise reached eminence.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ming and father Qian served Wei and both rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 琳母嘗祓禊泗濱，遇見一石，光彩朗潤，遂持以歸。

translations.literal: Lin's mother once performed the river purification rite on the Si bank; she encountered a stone, bright and lustrous, and took it home.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's mother once performed the river purification rite on the Si bank, found a bright, lustrous stone, and took it home.

sentences.zh: 是夜夢見一人，衣冠有若仙者，謂其母曰：「夫人向所將來之石，是浮磬之精。

translations.literal: That night she dreamed of a man, robed and capped like an immortal, who said to her: "The stone the lady brought back is the essence of the floating chime-stone.
translations.idiomatic: That night she dreamed of a robed, immortal-like man who told her, "The stone you brought back is the essence of a floating chime-stone.

sentences.zh: 若能寶持，必生令子。

translations.literal: If you can treasure and keep it, you will surely bear an outstanding son.
translations.idiomatic: Treasure it, and you will surely bear an outstanding son.

sentences.zh: 」其母驚寤，便舉身流汗，俄而有娠。

translations.literal: His mother started awake in alarm; her whole body broke out in sweat, and presently she conceived.
translations.idiomatic: She started awake in alarm, broke out in a sweat, and soon conceived.

sentences.zh: 及生，因名琳字季珉焉。

translations.literal: When he was born, he was therefore named Lin and styled Jimin.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born they therefore named him Lin and styled him Jimin.

sentences.zh: 魏正光初，起家衛府都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguang era of Wei, he began his career as a guard-office area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wei Zhenguang era he entered service as a guard-office area commander.

sentences.zh: 從元天穆討邢杲，破梁將

translations.literal: He followed Yuan Tianmu in suppressing Xing Gao, breaking the Liang general
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuan Tianmu against Xing Gao and defeated the Liang general

translations.literal: (Shen) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Shen]

sentences.zh: 〔陳〕慶之，以功轉統軍。

translations.literal: 〔Chen〕 [emended: Shen] Qingzhi; through merit he was transferred to army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi, and for his merit was made army commander.

sentences.zh: 又從爾朱天光破万俟醜奴，論功為最，除寧朔將軍、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He again followed Erzhu Tianguang in defeating Wan Qidu Chounu; his merit was rated highest; appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Erzhu Tianguang in defeating Wan Qidu Chounu, won top credit, and was made General Who Pacifies the North and commandant of the imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 後隨天光敗於韓陵山，琳因留洛陽。

translations.literal: Later, when he followed Tianguang and was defeated at Hanling Mountain, Lin remained at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tianguang was defeated at Hanling Mountain, Lin stayed behind in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，從入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he followed in entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he followed him through the passes.

sentences.zh: 至溱水，為齊神武所追，拒戰有功，封鉅野縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the Zhen River he was pursued by Gao Huan; resisting battle he had merit, and was enfeoffed Baron of Juye County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhen River he was pursued by Gao Huan; fighting a rearguard action with merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Juye County with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵為侯，增邑四百戶，轉龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, advanced to marquis; fief increased by four hundred households; transferred to General of Dragon Might.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was raised to marquis, given four hundred more households, and made General of Dragon Might.

sentences.zh: 頃之，授直閣將軍，遷平西將軍，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Direct Palace General and promoted to General Who Pacifies the West, with added Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made direct palace general and General Who Pacifies the West, with regular attendant of unimpeded access.

sentences.zh: 三年，從太祖破齊神武於沙苑，轉安西將軍，進爵為公，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the Grand Progenitor in defeating Gao Huan at Shaye; transferred to General Who Pacifies the West; advanced to duke; fief increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Gao Huan at Shaye, was made General Who Pacifies the West, raised to duke, and given eight hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 累遷衛將軍、銀青光祿大夫、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotion he rose to Guard General, Silver Grandee of the Splendid Dawn, and Right Grandee of the Splendid Dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to guard general, silver grandee of the splendid dawn, and right grandee of the splendid dawn.

sentences.zh: 四年，從擒莫多婁貸文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in capturing Moduolou Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he helped capture Moduolou Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 仍戰河橋，琳先驅奮擊，勇冠諸軍。

translations.literal: He again fought at River Bridge; Lin as vanguard charged fiercely; his courage topped the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at River Bridge; Lin led the vanguard in a fierce charge and his courage topped every army.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，謂之曰：「公卽我之韓、白也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor praised him and said to him: "Sir, you are my Han Xin and Bai Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him and said, "You are my Han Xin and Bai Qi.

sentences.zh: 」拜太子左庶子。

translations.literal: " Appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: Soon, in his former office, he garrisoned Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his rank, he garrisoned Yubi.

sentences.zh: 復從太祖戰邙山，除正平郡

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand Progenitor in battle at Mount Mang and was made Administrator of Zhengping commandery
translations.idiomatic: He again fought with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai at Mount Mang and was made administrator of Zhengping commandery

sentences.zh: （中正）

translations.literal: (Zhongzheng) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Zhongzheng]

sentences.zh: 〔守〕，加大都督，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: 〔Shou〕 [emended: Zhongzheng]; given the title grand area commander; fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: commandery administrator [emended from zhongzheng]; grand area commander; three hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 齊將東方老來寇，琳率衆禦之。

translations.literal: When Qi general Dongfang Lao came to raid, Lin led the host to repel him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi general Dongfang Lao raided, Lin led the troops to repel him.

sentences.zh: 老恃其勇健，直前趣琳。

translations.literal: Lao relied on his courage and strength and pressed straight toward Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lao trusted his strength and pressed straight at Lin.

sentences.zh: 短兵接，琳擊之，老中數瘡而退，謂其左右曰：「吾經陣多矣，未見如此健兒。

translations.literal: At close quarters Lin struck him; Lao received several wounds and withdrew, telling those beside him: "I have been through many battles, yet never seen such a stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: At close quarters Lin struck him; Lao took several wounds and withdrew, telling his men, "I have fought in many battles, but never seen such a fighting man.

sentences.zh: 」後乃密使人勸琳東歸，琳斬其使以聞。

translations.literal: " Later he secretly sent men to urge Lin to return east; Lin executed the envoys and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he secretly sent men to urge Lin to defect east; Lin executed the envoys and reported it.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Promoted to Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three-Duke honors, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bearer of the staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three-Duke honors, and regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 除鄜州刺史，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中。

translations.literal: Appointed Inspector of Mei Province; given Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Mei Province, with grand general of agile cavalry, grand master of the palace with Three-Duke rank, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵犍為郡公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Jianwei commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was raised to Duke of Jianwei commandery with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成初，從賀蘭祥征吐谷渾，以勳別封一子許昌縣公，邑一千戶，除延州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he followed Helan Xiang in campaigning against Tuyuhun; for merit a son was separately enfeoffed Duke of Xuchang County with a fief of one thousand households; appointed Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wucheng he followed Helan Xiang against Tuyuhun; for merit one son was separately enfeoffed Duke of Xuchang County with one thousand households, and he was made inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 又從柱國豆盧甯討稽胡郝阿保、劉桑德等，破之。

translations.literal: He again followed the pillar-of-state Doulu Ning in suppressing the Ji barbarians Hao Abao, Liu Sangde, and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed pillar-of-state Doulu Ning against the Ji barbarians Hao Abao, Liu Sangde, and others and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 二年，文州氐酋反，詔琳率兵討平之。

translations.literal: In the second year the Di chieftains of Wen Province rebelled; an edict ordered Lin to lead troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Di chieftains of Wen Province rebelled; Lin was ordered to lead troops and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 師還，帝宴羣公卿士，仍命賦詩言志。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor feasted the assembled nobles and ministers and also ordered them to compose poems expressing their intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor feasted the nobles and ministers and ordered them to compose poems on their aspirations.

sentences.zh: 琳詩末章云：「寄言竇車騎，為謝霍將軍，何以報天子？

translations.literal: The final stanza of Lin's poem said: "Send word to General of Agile Cavalry Dou, and thank General Huo—how shall we repay the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The final stanza of Lin's poem ran, "Send word to General of Agile Cavalry Dou, and thank General Huo—how shall we repay the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 沙漠靜妖氛。

translations.literal: The desert's baleful mists are stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Baleful mists over the desert lie still.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅曰：「獯獫陸梁，未時款塞，卿言有驗，國之福也。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "The Xiongnu are unruly and have not yet come to pledge allegiance at the frontier; your words have proof—this is the realm's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "The Xiongnu are still unruly and have not yet submitted at the frontier; your words have been proved—this is the realm's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 子儒，少以父勳賜爵許昌

translations.literal: His son Ru, while young through his father's merit was granted noble rank of Xuchang
translations.idiomatic: His son Ru, while still young, was enfeoffed at Xuchang for his father's merit

translations.literal: (Commandery) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: commandery]

sentences.zh: 〔縣〕公，拜左侍上士。

translations.literal: 〔County〕 [emended: commandery] duke, appointed Left Attendant Upper Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuchang county and made Left Attendant Upper Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵犍為郡公，位至儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Jianwei commandery and reached Honorary Peer Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded as Duke of Jianwei and rose to Honorary Peer Grand General.

sentences.zh: 李和本名慶和，其先隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li He originally bore the name Qinghe; his forebears were men of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li He was born Qinghe; his family came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 後徙居朔方。

translations.literal: Later they moved and settled in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: The clan later relocated to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 父僧養，以累世雄豪，善於統御，為夏州酋長。

translations.literal: His father Sengyang, through generations of local power, was skilled at command and became chieftain of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyang, a hereditary strongman skilled in leadership, became chieftain of Xia.

sentences.zh: 和少敢勇，有識度，狀貌魁偉，為州里所推。

translations.literal: He in youth was bold and brave, had judgment and measure, his form tall and imposing, and was promoted by the district.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Li He was daring and clear-sighted, tall and imposing, and widely respected in the region.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳作鎮關中，乃引和為帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue held the garrison in Guanzhong, he then brought He in as commander within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue governed Guanzhong, he took Li He into his personal staff as tent commander.

sentences.zh: 以破諸賊功，稍遷征北將軍、金紫光祿大夫，賜爵思陽公。

translations.literal: For merit in breaking the various bandits, he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn, and enfeoffed as Duke of Siyang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit against the bandits brought him step by step to General Who Pacifies the North and Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn, with the title Duke of Siyang.

sentences.zh: 尋除漢陽郡守。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Administrator of Hanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 治存寬簡，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: His governance preserved leniency and simplicity; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and restraint, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 至大統初，加車騎將軍、左光祿大夫、都督，累遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍、侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、夏州刺史，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Datong, he was given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grandee of Glorious Affairs, and area commander; he was promoted in succession to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Scattered Cavalry, Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Xia Province, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he received the ranks of General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grandee of Glorious Affairs, and area commander, then rose through Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, became inspector of Xia, and was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂諸將曰：「宇文慶和，智略明贍，立身恭謹，累經委任，每稱吾意。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once said to the generals: "Yuwen Qinghe is wise in plan and bright in resource; he stands in life with reverent care; repeatedly entrusted with office, he each time accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told his officers, "Yuwen Qinghe is shrewd and dependable; in every post I have given him he has done exactly as I wished.

sentences.zh: 」遂賜名意焉。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon given the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " So he was given the personal name Yi.

sentences.zh: 改封永豐縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yongfeng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Yongfeng with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，除司憲中大夫，進爵義城郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he was removed and made Middle Grandee of the Court of Justice, and advanced in rank to Duke of Yicheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he became Middle Grandee of the Court of Justice and was raised to Duke of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 尋又改封德廣郡公，出為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was again changed to Duke of Deguang commandery, and he went out as Inspector of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Duke of Deguang and sent out as inspector of Luo.

sentences.zh: 和前在夏州，頗留遺惠，及有此授，商洛父老，莫不想望德音。

translations.literal: He before this had been at Xia Province and had left much lingering kindness; when he received this appointment, the elders of Shang and Luo, none did not long for his virtuous voice.
translations.idiomatic: During his earlier tenure at Xia he had left the people with lasting goodwill; when this new appointment came, elders throughout Shang and Luo looked to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 和至州，以仁恕訓物，獄訟為之簡靜。

translations.literal: When He reached the prefecture, with benevolence and forbearance he instructed the people, and lawsuits thereby became few and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: At Luo he governed with mercy and restraint, and the courts grew calm.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，進位大將軍，拜延綏丹三州武安伏夷安民三防諸軍事、延州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was advanced to grand general and appointed to all military affairs of the three garrisons Wuan, Fuyi, and Anmin in the three prefectures Yan, Sui, and Dan, and Inspector of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 3 he was made grand general and given command of Yan, Sui, and Dan, with authority over the Wuan, Fuyi, and Anmin garrisons, and became inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 六年，進柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to pillar-of-state grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，改授延綏銀三州文安伏夷安民周昌梁和五防諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande, he was reassigned to all military affairs of the five garrisons Wen'an, Fuyi, Anmin, Zhouchang, and Lianghe in the three prefectures Yan, Sui, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 1 his command was changed to Yan, Sui, and Yin, with authority over the five garrisons Wen'an, Fuyi, Anmin, Zhouchang, and Lianghe.

sentences.zh: 以罪免。

translations.literal: For crime he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋復柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to pillar-of-state rank.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，遷上柱國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sui Kaichu, he was transferred to supreme pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Kaichu year 1 he was made supreme pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 和立身剛簡，老而逾勵，諸子趨事，若奉嚴君。

translations.literal: He in person was upright and austere; in old age he grew only more strenuous; his sons in attending to affairs were as if serving a stern lord.
translations.idiomatic: Li He remained upright and austere to the end, growing only stricter with age; his sons served him as though he were a severe father.

sentences.zh: 以意是太祖賜名，市朝已革，慶和則父之所命，義不可違。

translations.literal: Because Yi was a name the Grand Progenitor had granted, and the market and court had already changed, while Qinghe was what his father had commanded—righteousness could not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had been a name given by Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, but the dynasty had changed; Qinghe was his father's gift, and that bond could not be set aside.

sentences.zh: 至是，遂以和為名。

translations.literal: At this time, he thereupon took He as his name.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore resumed the name He.

sentences.zh: 二年，薨，贈本官，加司徒公、徐兗邳沂海泗六州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he died; he was granted his former office plus Duke of the Minister of Education and Inspector of the six prefectures Xu, Yan, Pi, Yi, Hai, and Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died and was posthumously given his former rank plus Duke of the Minister of Education and inspector of six prefectures including Xu, Yan, Pi, Yi, Hai, and Si.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Su (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 子徹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Che succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 伊婁穆

translations.literal: Yi Lou Mu
translations.idiomatic: Yi Lou Mu (伊婁穆)

sentences.zh: 伊婁穆字奴干，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Lou Mu, styled Nugan, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Lou Mu, styled Nugan, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父靈，善騎射，為太祖所知。

translations.literal: His father Ling was skilled at mounted archery and was known to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling was an expert horse-archer and came to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's notice.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗謂之曰：「昔伊尹保衡於殷，致主堯舜。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once said to him: "In old times Yi Yin and Baoding guarded Yin and brought their lord to the level of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told him, "Long ago Yi Yin and Baoding served Yin and raised their ruler to the level of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 卿旣姓伊，庶卿不替前緒。

translations.literal: You already bear the surname Yi; I hope you will not fail your forebears' thread.
translations.idiomatic: Your surname is already Yi; I trust you will not fall short of that legacy.

sentences.zh: 」於是賜名尹焉。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon given the name Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore given the personal name Yin.

sentences.zh: 歷金紫光祿大夫、衛將軍、隆州刺史，賜爵盧奴縣公。

translations.literal: He passed through Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn, Guard General, and Inspector of Long Prefecture, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lunu county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn, Guard General, and inspector of Long, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lunu.

sentences.zh: 穆弱冠為太祖內親信，以機辯見知，授奉朝請，常侍左右。

translations.literal: Mu at weak-crown age became the Grand Progenitor's inner trusted attendant; through quick wit and eloquence he was known, was appointed Court Gentleman for Palace Service, and constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties Mu became one of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's personal attendants; his quick wit won notice, and he was made Court Gentleman for Palace Service and kept constantly at the Grand Progenitor's side.

sentences.zh: 邙山之役，力戰有功，拜子都督、丞相府參軍事，轉外兵參軍。

translations.literal: In the Battle of Mount Mang he fought hard with merit, was appointed junior area commander and staff officer in the chancellor's office, and was transferred to external-army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang he fought fiercely and well, was made junior area commander and staff officer in the chancellor's office, then transferred to the external-army staff.

sentences.zh: 累遷帥都督、平東將軍、中散大夫，歷中書舍人、尚書駕部郎中、撫軍將軍、大都督、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to area commander, General Who Pacifies the East, and Palace Grandee of the Scattered Cavalry, and passed through Secretariat Draftsman, Bureau Chief of the Chariot Office in the Ministry of Works, General Who Pacifies the Army, grand area commander, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Direct Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through area commander, General Who Pacifies the East, and Palace Grandee of the Scattered Cavalry, then served as secretariat draftsman, bureau chief of the Chariot Office, General Who Pacifies the Army, grand area commander, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Direct Transmission.

sentences.zh: 嘗入白事，太祖望見悅之，字之曰：「奴干作儀同面見我矣。

translations.literal: Once when he entered to report business, the Grand Progenitor saw him from afar and was pleased with him, addressing him by style: "Nugan, you have risen to Honorary Peer rank to meet my face.
translations.idiomatic: Once, entering to report, he was seen from afar by Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, who was delighted and said by his style, "Nugan, you have made Honorary Peer rank and come before me in person.

sentences.zh: 」於是拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，賜封安陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " He was at once made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed Baron of Anyang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉大丞相府掾，遷從事中郎，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to staff officer in the Grand Chancellor's office, promoted to Attendant Gentleman, and removed as Chief of the Yellow Gate, Attendant-in-Service.
translations.idiomatic: He became a staff officer in the Grand Chancellor's office, rose to Attendant Gentleman, and was appointed Chief of the Yellow Gate, Attendant-in-Service.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，穆使於蜀。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, Mu was sent as envoy to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Deposed Emperor of Wei year 2 Mu was sent on mission to Shu.

sentences.zh: 屬伍城郡人趙雄傑與梓潼郡人王令公、鄧朏等構逆，衆三萬餘人，阻涪水立柵，進逼潼州。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhao Xiongjie of Wucheng commandery with Wang Linggong of Zitong commandery, Deng Fei, and others plotted rebellion; the host was more than thirty thousand men; they blocked the Fu River and built stockades, advancing to press Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiongjie of Wucheng and Wang Linggong of Zitong, together with Deng Fei and others, rebelled with more than thirty thousand men, fortified the Fu River, and pressed Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 穆遂與刺史叱羅協率兵破之。

translations.literal: Mu thereupon with Inspector Chiluo Xie led troops and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Mu joined Inspector Chiluo Xie, routed the rebels, and relieved the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was enlarged by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜兵部中大夫，治御正，進爵為侯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed Middle Grandee of the Ministry of War, administering the Bureau of Imperial Rectification, advanced in rank to marquis, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Mu became Middle Grandee of the Ministry of War with charge of the Bureau of Imperial Rectification, was raised to marquis, and gained five hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 尋進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 保定初，授軍司馬，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was appointed Army Master of Horse and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he became Army Master of Horse and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 四年，除金州總管、八州諸軍事、金州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was removed as Military Commissioner of Jin, with military affairs of eight prefectures, and Inspector of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made military commissioner of Jin with authority over eight prefectures and became inspector of Jin.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，增邑二千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, his fief was increased by two thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 his fief grew by twenty-one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又為民部中大夫。

translations.literal: He was again made Middle Grandee of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Middle Grandee of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 衛公直出鎮襄州，以穆為長史。

translations.literal: When Duke of Wei Zhi went out to hold Xiang Prefecture, Mu was made chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Wei Zhi took command at Xiang, Mu became his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 郢州城民王道肯反，襲據州城。

translations.literal: Wang Daoken, a townsman of Ying Prefecture city, rebelled and by surprise seized the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daoken, a resident of Ying city, rebelled and seized the prefectural seat by surprise.

sentences.zh: 直遣穆率百餘騎馳往援之。

translations.literal: Zhi dispatched Mu to lead more than a hundred horsemen in rapid ride to go to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent Mu with a little over a hundred horsemen to ride to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 穆至城下，頻破肯衆。

translations.literal: When Mu reached below the city, he repeatedly broke Ken's host.
translations.idiomatic: Below the walls Mu broke Daoken's force again and again.

sentences.zh: 會大將軍高琳率衆軍繼進，肯等乃降。

translations.literal: It happened that Grand General Gao Lin led the mass of armies in continued advance; Ken and the others thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Gao Lin then arrived with the main army, and Daoken surrendered.

sentences.zh: 唐州山蠻恃險逆命，穆率軍討之。

translations.literal: The mountain barbarians of Tang Prefecture relied on the terrain and defied orders; Mu led an army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain tribes of Tang relied on rough country and refused submission; Mu marched against them.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋等保據石窟一十四處，穆分軍進討，旬有四日，竝破之，虜獲六千五百人。

translations.literal: The barbarian chiefs and others held fast in fourteen stone grottoes; Mu divided the army and advanced in attack; in ten days plus four, all were broken together; captives taken numbered six thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs held fourteen cliff caves; Mu split his force and attacked; in fourteen days all were taken, with sixty-five hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 建德初。
