translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 授荊州，復以穆為總管府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed to Jing Prefecture, and again Mu was made chief clerk of the military commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was reassigned, Mu was again made chief clerk of the military commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 穆頻貳戚藩，甚得匡贊之譽。

translations.literal: Mu repeatedly served as second to imperial princes and greatly gained a reputation for loyal support.
translations.idiomatic: Serving repeatedly as deputy to imperial princes, Mu won wide praise for steady counsel.

sentences.zh: 入為小司馬。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Master of Horse.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Junior Master of Horse.

sentences.zh: 從柱國李穆平軹關等城，賞布帛三百疋、粟三百石、田三十頃。

translations.literal: He followed Pillar-of-State Li Mu in pacifying the cities of Zhi Pass and others; he was rewarded with three hundred bolts of cloth and silk, three hundred shi of grain, and thirty qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Pillar-of-State Li Mu in taking Zhi Pass and neighboring cities and was rewarded with three hundred bolts of silk, three hundred shi of grain, and thirty qing of land.

sentences.zh: 五年，從皇太子討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he followed the Crown Prince in campaigning against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the Crown Prince's campaign against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 還，穆殿，為渾人圍。

translations.literal: On return, Mu brought up the rear and was surrounded by Tuyuhun men.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Mu commanded the rearguard and was surrounded by Tuyuhun forces.

sentences.zh: 會劉雄救至，乃得解。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Xiong's rescue arrived, and he was then able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong arrived with relief, and he broke free.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 楊紹字子安，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Shao, styled Zi'an, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shao, styled Zi'an, came from Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖興，魏新平郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing was Administrator of Xinping commandery in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing had been administrator of Xinping under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父國，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Guo was Palace Grandee of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guo had served as palace grandee of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 紹少慷慨有志略，屢從征伐，力戰有功。

translations.literal: Shao in youth was generous and resolute with ambition and plan; repeatedly he followed campaigns, fighting hard with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yang Shao was bold and far-sighted; he fought in many campaigns and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，授廣武將軍、屯騎校尉、直蕩別將。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an period of Wei, he was appointed General of Broad Might, Commandant of the Wagon-and-Horse, and Separate Commander of Direct Advance.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yong'an era he was made General of Broad Might, Commandant of the Wagon-and-Horse, and Separate Commander of Direct Advance.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，封平鄉男，邑一百戶，加征西將軍，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingxiang with a fief of one hundred households, and further given General Who Conquers the West and Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Putai he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang with one hundred households and also given General Who Conquers the West and Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn.

sentences.zh: 復從大將軍達奚武征漢中。

translations.literal: He again followed Grand General Daxi Wu in campaigning against Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Grand General Daxi Wu's campaign against Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時梁宜豐侯蕭循固守梁州。

translations.literal: At the time Liang's Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, firmly held Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xun, was then holding Liang Province in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 紹以為懸軍敵境，圍守堅城，曠日持久，糧饟不繼，城中若致死於我，懼不能歸，請為計以誘之。

translations.literal: Shao considered that with the army suspended in enemy territory, besieging and holding a strong city, days and months prolonged, grain and fodder not continuing, if within the city they were to fight to the death against us, he feared they could not return; he requested a plan to lure them out.
translations.idiomatic: Shao argued that an army deep in enemy country, pinning a strong city while supplies ran out, risked a desperate sally they might not survive; he asked leave to lure the defenders out.

sentences.zh: 乃頻至城下挑戰，設伏待之。

translations.literal: He thereupon repeatedly went below the city to challenge battle and set ambushes to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He rode repeatedly to the walls to offer battle and laid ambushes nearby.

sentences.zh: 循初不肯出。

translations.literal: At first Xun would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiao Xun refused to sally.

sentences.zh: 紹又遣人罵辱之，循怒，果出兵，紹率衆偽退。

translations.literal: Shao again sent men to revile and insult him; Xun grew angry, and indeed sent out troops; Shao led the host in feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to hurl abuse; Xun, enraged, marched out, and Shao feigned retreat with his troops.

sentences.zh: 城降。

translations.literal: The city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 以功授輔國將軍、中散大夫，聽回授一子。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed General Who Supports the State and Palace Grandee of the Scattered Cavalry, and permitted to transfer the honor to one son.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was made General Who Supports the State and Palace Grandee of the Scattered Cavalry, with permission to pass the honor to a son.

sentences.zh: 又從柱國、燕國公于謹圍江陵。

translations.literal: He again followed Pillar-of-State, Duke of Yan, Yu Jin in besieging Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Pillar-of-State Yu Jin, Duke of Yan, in the siege of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 紹鬬於枇杷門，流矢中股而力戰不衰。

translations.literal: Shao fought at Pipa Gate; a flying arrow struck his thigh, yet he fought hard without decline.
translations.idiomatic: At Pipa Gate an arrow struck his thigh, yet Yang Shao fought on without slackening.

sentences.zh: 事平，賞奴婢一百口，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，除衡州刺史，賜姓叱利氏。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was rewarded with one hundred male and female slaves, advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, removed as Inspector of Heng Prefecture, and granted the surname Chilu.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he received one hundred slaves, was raised to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, made inspector of Heng, and granted the surname Chilu.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，卒，贈成文等八州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he died; posthumously granted Inspector of the eight prefectures including Cheng and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he died and was posthumously made inspector of eight prefectures including Cheng and Wen.

sentences.zh: 諡曰信。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xin (Trustworthy).

sentences.zh: 子雄嗣，大象末，上柱國、邽國公。

translations.literal: His son Xiong succeeded; at the end of Daxiang, he was supreme pillar-of-state and Duke of Gui state.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong succeeded him; by the end of Daxiang he was supreme pillar-of-state and Duke of Gui.

sentences.zh: 王雅字度容，闡熙新

translations.literal: Wang Ya, styled Durong, was of Chanxi Xin
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, styled Durong, came from Chanxi Xin

translations.literal: (Gu) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Gu]

sentences.zh: 〔囶〕人也。

translations.literal: 〔Enclosure character 囶〕 [emended: Gu] native.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Chanxi Xingu.

sentences.zh: 少而沉毅，木訥寡言，有膽勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep and resolute, wooden and slow of speech and sparing of words, had courage and bravery, and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wang Ya was grave and steady, taciturn, brave, and expert at horse-archery.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其名，召入軍，累有戰功。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard his name and summoned him into the army; repeatedly he had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard of him, called him into service, and he won repeated honors in battle.

sentences.zh: 除都督，賜爵居庸縣子。

translations.literal: He was removed as area commander and enfeoffed as Viscount of Juyong county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made area commander and enfeoffed Viscount of Juyong.

sentences.zh: 東魏將竇泰入寇，雅從太祖擒之于潼關。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei's general Dou Tai entered in invasion, Ya followed the Grand Progenitor in capturing him at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei's general Dou Tai invaded, Wang Ya followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and helped capture him at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之戰，雅謂所部曰：「彼軍殆有百萬，今我不滿萬人，以常理論之，實難與敵。

translations.literal: In the Battle of Shaye, Ya said to his command: "That army is likely near a million; now we are not full ten thousand men; by ordinary reason to discuss it, truly it is hard to match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaye Wang Ya told his troops, "They may field near a million men while we are fewer than ten thousand; by ordinary reckoning we cannot stand against them.

sentences.zh: 但相公神武命世，股肱王室，以順討逆，豈計衆寡。

translations.literal: But the Prime Minister is divinely martial and destined for the age, arm and thigh of the royal house; to raise right in punishing rebellion—how could one count numbers?
translations.idiomatic: But our Prime Minister is divinely martial, the royal house's mainstay—when the righteous march against rebels, who counts numbers?

sentences.zh: 丈夫若不以此時破賊，何用生為！

translations.literal: If a man does not at this time break the bandits, what use is living!
translations.idiomatic: If a man won't break the enemy now, what use is living!

sentences.zh: 」乃擐甲步戰，所向披靡，太祖壯之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon donned armor and fought on foot; wherever he turned, enemies were swept aside; the Grand Progenitor admired him.
translations.idiomatic: " He buckled on armor and fought on foot, cutting through every line; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was impressed.

sentences.zh: 又從戰邙山。

translations.literal: He again followed in battle at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 時大軍不利，為敵所乘，諸將皆引退，雅獨回騎拒之。

translations.literal: At that time the main army was unfavorable and was exploited by the enemy; the various generals all withdrew, but Ya alone wheeled his horse back and resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force faltered and the enemy pressed its advantage, every general fell back except Ya, who turned his horse and held them off.

sentences.zh: 敵人見其無繼，步騎競進。

translations.literal: The enemy, seeing he had no support, infantry and cavalry vied to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he had no reinforcements, the enemy infantry and cavalry surged forward together.

sentences.zh: 雅左右奮擊，頻斬九級，敵衆稍卻，雅乃還軍。

translations.literal: To left and right of Ya they fought hard; nine heads were repeatedly cut off; the enemy host slightly retreated, and Ya then returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He and his companions fought fiercely, taking nine heads in succession; the enemy fell back a little, and Ya rejoined the army.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「王雅舉身悉是膽也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed and said: "Wang Ya—his whole body is gall.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sighed and said, "Wang Ya is nothing but gall from head to foot.

sentences.zh: 」錄前後功，進爵為伯，除帥都督、鄜城郡守。

translations.literal: " His merits before and after were recorded; he was advanced in rank to baron and removed as commander-in-chief and made Administrator of Fucheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " For his services before and after, he was raised to baron, made commander-in-chief, and appointed administrator of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 政尚簡易，吏人安之。

translations.literal: His governance favored simplicity and ease; officials and people were settled by it.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with plain simplicity, and officials and people alike were at ease.

sentences.zh: 遷大都督、延州刺史，轉夏州刺史，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand area commander and Inspector of Yan Prefecture, changed to Inspector of Xia Prefecture, given Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand area commander and inspector of Yan, then inspector of Xia; he received the ranks of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除汾州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was removed as Inspector of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was made inspector of Fen.

sentences.zh: 勵精為治，人庶悅而附之，自遠至者七百餘家。

translations.literal: He exerted spirit in governance; the people rejoiced and attached themselves; from afar who came numbered more than seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into good government; the people gladly rallied to him, and more than seven hundred households came from distant places to settle.

sentences.zh: 保定初，復為夏州刺史，卒于州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he again became Inspector of Xia Prefecture and died in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoding he returned as inspector of Xia and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子世積嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shiji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有文武幹略。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and had civil and military capacity and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shiji was bold and capable in both letters and arms.

sentences.zh: 大象末，上大將軍、宜陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached Supreme Grand General and Duke of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang he had risen to supreme grand general and Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 達奚寔

translations.literal: Da Xishi
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi (達奚寔)

sentences.zh: 達奚寔字什伏代，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Da Xishi, styled Shifudai, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi, styled Shifudai, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 高祖涼州，魏征西將軍、山陽公。

translations.literal: His high ancestor [of] Liang Province, Wei General Who Conquers the West and Duke of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His high ancestor had served as inspector of Liang and held the Wei rank of General Who Conquers the West and Duke of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 父顯相，武衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xiansiang was General of Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiansiang was General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 寔少修立，有幹局。

translations.literal: Shi in youth cultivated upright conduct and had capacity and scope.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi in youth was upright and capable.

sentences.zh: 起家給事中，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Within the Palace, with added General Who Conquers the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an attendant within the palace and was given the added rank of General Who Conquers the Champions.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，授都督，鎮弘農。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was granted area commander and garrisoned Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he was made area commander and posted to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 後從西遷，封臨汾縣伯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed the move west, was enfeoffed as Baron of Linfen county with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the western removal he was enfeoffed Baron of Linfen with six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷大行臺郎中，仍與行臺郎神鎮潼關。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director of the Grand Commissionerate, and still together with Langshen, commissionerate gentleman, garrisoned Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He became bureau director of the grand commissionerate and still garrisoned Tong Pass together with Langshen of the commissionerate staff.

sentences.zh: 及潼關失守，卽與大都督陽山武戰于關，東魏人甚憚之。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass fell, he at once with Grand Area Commander Yang Shanwu fought at the pass; Eastern Wei men greatly feared them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell he fought at the pass alongside Grand Area Commander Yang Shanwu, and the Eastern Wei forces feared them greatly.

sentences.zh: 從太祖擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，皆力戰有功，增邑三百戶，加車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor he captured Dou Tai, recovered Hongnong, and broke Shaye—in each he fought hard with merit; his fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was given General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grandee of Glorious Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Following Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai he helped capture Dou Tai, retake Hongnong, and win at Shaye, earning credit in each fight; his fief rose by three hundred households, and he received General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grandee of Glorious Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又授大行臺郎中、相府掾，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was again granted Bureau Director of the Grand Commissionerate and Staff Member of the Chancellor's Office, and transferred to Attendant Gentleman-of-the-Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was again made bureau director of the grand commissionerate and staff member of the chancellor's office, then transferred to attendant gentleman-of-the-palace.

sentences.zh: 寔性嚴重，太祖深器之。

translations.literal: Shi's nature was stern and grave; the Grand Progenitor deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi was stern and weighty in character, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 累遷大都督、持節、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Area Commander, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and Regular Attendant through Direct Connection of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to grand area commander, bearer of the staff of authority, and regular attendant through direct connection of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，除中外府司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, he was removed as army marshal of the Central and External Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Deposed Emperor year 2 he was made army marshal of the central and external office.

sentences.zh: 大軍伐蜀，以寔行南岐州事，兼都軍糧。

translations.literal: The main army campaigned against Shu; Shi was made to conduct the affairs of Southern Qi Prefecture and concurrently oversee all army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force marched on Shu, Da Xishi was put in charge of Southern Qi and also directed all army provisions.

sentences.zh: 先是，山氐生獷，不供賦役，歷世羈縻，莫能制御。

translations.literal: Before this, the mountain Di were fierce by nature, did not supply taxes and labor service, through generations were loosely bridled, and none could control them.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the mountain Di were wild and refused taxes and corvée; for generations they had been loosely controlled, and no one could subdue them.

sentences.zh: 寔導之以政，氐人感悅，竝從賦稅。

translations.literal: Shi guided them with governance; the Di people were moved and rejoiced, and all followed with taxes and grain tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xishi governed them patiently; the Di were moved and willingly paid taxes and tribute.

sentences.zh: 於是大軍糧餼，咸取給焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the main army's grain rations all took supply from there.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the army drew its provisions from them.

sentences.zh: 尋徵還，仍為司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back and still served as army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and resumed his post as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜蕃部中大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵平陽縣公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Middle Grandee of the Barbarian Department, given Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and advanced in rank to Duke of Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he became Middle Grandee of the Barbarian Department, received Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, and was raised to Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，授禦正中大夫，治民部，兼晉公護司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, he was granted Middle Grandee of Correct Attendance, administered the People Department, and concurrently served as army marshal to Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he was made Middle Grandee of Correct Attendance, head of the People Department, and also served as army marshal to Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，出為文州刺史，卒于州，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he went out as Inspector of Wen Prefecture, died in the prefecture; his age was then forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 1 he was sent out as inspector of Wen and died there at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈文康二州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Inspector of the two prefectures Wen and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Wen and Kang.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Gong (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 子豐嗣。

translations.literal: His son Feng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 劉雄字猛雀，臨洮子城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiong, styled Mengque, was a man of Zicheng in Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong, styled Mengque, came from Zicheng in Lintao.

sentences.zh: 少機辯，慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and eloquent, magnanimous and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Liu Xiong was quick-witted and eloquent, open-handed and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 大統中，起家為太祖親信。

translations.literal: In Datong, he began his career as the Grand Progenitor's trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong he entered service as a trusted aide of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 尋授統軍、宣威將軍、給事中，除子城令，加都督、輔國將軍、中散大夫，兼中書舍人，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted army commander, General Who Proclaims Might, and Attendant Within the Palace; removed as Magistrate of Zicheng; given area commander, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Attendant Scattered Within; concurrently made Palace Secretariat Attendant; and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made army commander, General Who Proclaims Might, and palace attendant, appointed magistrate of Zicheng, given the added ranks of area commander, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Attendant Scattered Within, made concurrent palace secretariat attendant, and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，加大都督，曆司市下大夫，齊右下大夫，治小駕部，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was given grand area commander, successively served as Lower Grandee of the Market Office, Lower Right Grandee of Qi, administered the Minor Escort Department, and advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne he was made grand area commander, served as Lower Grandee of the Market Office and Lower Right Grandee of Qi, headed the Minor Escort Department, and rose to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，治中外府屬，從征洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he administered the staff of the Central and External Office and followed the campaign to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he served on the staff of the central and external office and joined the Luoyang campaign.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，遷駕部中大夫，四年，兼齊公憲府掾，從憲出宜陽，築安義等城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, he was transferred to Middle Grandee of the Chariot Department; in the fourth year, concurrently Staff Member of Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian's office; he followed Xian out to Yiyang and built the cities Anyi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 he became Middle Grandee of the Chariot Department; in year 4 he also served on Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian's staff, followed Xian to Yiyang, and built cities including Anyi.

sentences.zh: 五年，齊相斛律明月率衆築通關城以援宜陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Qi chancellor Hulu Mingyue led a host to build Tongguan City to aid Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Northern Qi's chancellor Hulu Mingyue led troops to build Tongguan city in support of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，國家與齊通好，約言各保境息民，不相侵擾。

translations.literal: Before this, the state and Qi had open communication and friendship; they agreed in words that each should keep to its borders and give the people rest, not invading and harassing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the two states were at peace with Qi, having pledged to keep to their borders and leave the people in peace.

sentences.zh: 至是，憲以齊人失信，令雄使于明月，責其背約。

translations.literal: At this time, Xian because the Qi people had broken faith, ordered Xiong as envoy to Mingyue to rebuke them for betraying the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, holding Qi in breach of faith, sent Liu Xiong as envoy to Hulu Mingyue to denounce the broken pact.

sentences.zh: 雄辭義辯直，齊人憚焉。

translations.literal: Xiong's words in meaning were eloquent and straight; the Qi people feared him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong spoke with force and frank eloquence, and the Qi side held him in awe.

sentences.zh: 使還，兼中

translations.literal: On return from the mission, he was also appointed Central
translations.idiomatic: On return from his mission he was also made a

translations.literal: (Office) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: office]

sentences.zh: 外〔府〕掾。

translations.literal: 〔External Office〕 [emended: Office] staff member.
translations.idiomatic: staff member of the central and external office.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封周昌縣伯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Baron of Zhoucheng county with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid State with Honorary Peer Three Excellencies and enfeoffed Baron of Zhoucheng with six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 齊人又于姚襄築伏龍等五城，以處戍卒。

translations.literal: The Qi people again at Yao Xiang built Fulong and other five cities to lodge garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces also built five garrison cities including Fulong at Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 雄從齊公憲攻之，五城皆拔。

translations.literal: Xiong followed Duke of Qi Xian in attacking them; all five cities were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong followed Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian in the attack and all five cities fell.

sentences.zh: 憲復遣雄與柱國宇文盛于齊長城已西，連營防禦。

translations.literal: Xian again sent Xiong with pillar-of-state Yuwen Sheng west of Qi's Great Wall to link camps in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then sent Liu Xiong with pillar-of-state Yuwen Sheng to link camps in defense west of the Qi Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 齊將段孝先等率衆圍盛。

translations.literal: Qi general Duan Xiaoxian and others led a host to besiege Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi general Duan Xiaoxian and others led troops to besiege Yuwen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 營外先有長塹，大將軍韓歡與孝先交戰不利，雄身負排，率所部二十餘人，據塹力戰，孝先等乃止。

translations.literal: Outside the camp there was already a long trench; Great General Han Huan fought Duan Xiaoxian unfavorably; Xiong on his body bore a shield, led his command of more than twenty men, held the trench and fought hard; Xiaoxian and the others then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A long trench lay outside the camp; when Great General Han Huan fought Duan Xiaoxian and faltered, Liu Xiong took up a shield himself, led a little over twenty men, and held the trench in hard fighting until Xiaoxian broke off.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遷軍司馬，進爵為侯，邑一千四百戶。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to army marshal, advanced in rank to marquis, with a fief of one thousand four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was made army marshal, raised to marquis, and given a fief of fourteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建德初，授納言，轉軍正，復為納言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he was granted Recorder, transferred to Army Rectifier, and again made Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiande he was made recorder, then army rectifier, and again recorder.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉內史中大夫，除

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Middle Grandee of the Masters of Writing, removed as
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was transferred to Middle Grandee of the Masters of Writing and appointed

translations.literal: (Marquis) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: marquis]

sentences.zh: 〔候〕正。

translations.literal: 〔Commandant〕 [emended: Marquis] rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: commandant.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗從容謂雄曰：「古人云：『富貴不歸故鄉，猶衣錦夜遊。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once leisurely said to Xiong: "The ancients said: 'Wealth and honor not returning to one's native place is like wearing brocade on a night stroll.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once said to Liu Xiong in an easy tone, "The ancients said, 'Wealth and honor that never return to one's home are like wearing brocade on a night walk.

sentences.zh: 』今以卿為本州，何如？

translations.literal: " Now to make you governor of your native prefecture—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: " How would you like to be made governor of your home province?

sentences.zh: 」雄稽首拜謝。

translations.literal: " Xiong prostrated himself and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Xiong kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以雄為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Xiong Inspector of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon made Liu Xiong inspector of He.

sentences.zh: 雄先已為本縣令，復有此授，鄉里榮之。

translations.literal: Xiong before this had already been magistrate of his native county; to again have this appointment—his village and district honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He had already served as magistrate of his home county, and this new honor brought glory to his home district.

sentences.zh: 四年，從柱國李穆出軹關，攻邵州等城，拔之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed pillar-of-state Li Mu out through Zhi Pass, attacked Shao Prefecture and other cities, and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he followed pillar-of-state Li Mu out through Zhi Pass, attacked Shao and other cities, and took them.

sentences.zh: 以功獲賞。

translations.literal: For merit he received reward.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded for his merit.

sentences.zh: 五

translations.literal: Five
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth

translations.literal: (Thousand) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: thousand]

sentences.zh: 〔年〕，皇太子西征吐谷渾，雄自涼州從滕王逌率軍先入渾境，去伏侯城二百餘里，逌遣雄先至城東舉火，與大軍相應。

translations.literal: 〔Year〕 [emended: Thousand], the Crown Prince campaigned west against Tuyuhun; Xiong from Liang Prefecture followed Prince of Teng Yu with the army, entering Tuyuhun territory first, more than two hundred li from Fuhou City; Yu sent Xiong ahead first to the east of the city to raise signal fires, responding with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: year, the Crown Prince marched west against Tuyuhun; Liu Xiong set out from Liang with Prince of Teng Yu, entered Tuyuhun territory first, and when still more than two hundred li from Fuhou city Yu sent him ahead to light signal fires east of the city to coordinate with the main force.

sentences.zh: 渾洮王率七百餘騎逆戰。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun's King of Tao led more than seven hundred horsemen to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun King of Tao met them with more than seven hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 雄時所部數百人先並分遣斥候，在左右者二十許人。

translations.literal: Xiong at that time had several hundred men under his command; first all were separately sent as scouts; at left and right were about twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong had only a few hundred men and had already sent out scouts; about twenty remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 雄卽率與交戰，斬首七十餘級，雄亦亡其三騎。

translations.literal: Xiong then led them in battle, cut off more than seventy heads; Xiong also lost three of his horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He led those men into battle, took more than seventy heads, and lost three horsemen of his own.

sentences.zh: 自是從逌連戰之，雄功居多，賞物甚厚。

translations.literal: From then he followed Yu in continuous battles; Xiong's merit was mostly the greatest; material rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he fought under Yu in one engagement after another; Liu Xiong's share of the credit was the largest, and his rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，伊婁穆殿，為賊所圍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yi Lou Mu brought up the rear and was surrounded by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Yi Lou Mu commanded the rearguard and was surrounded by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 皇太子命雄救之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ordered Xiong to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ordered Liu Xiong to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 雄率騎一千解穆圍。

translations.literal: Xiong led one thousand horsemen and relieved Mu's siege.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong led one thousand cavalry and broke the siege around Mu.

sentences.zh: 增邑三百戶，加上開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was given Supreme Opening-establishment Honorary Peer Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose by three hundred households and he received supreme opening-establishment honorary peer three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍東討，雄從齊王憲拔洪洞，下永安。

translations.literal: That year the main army campaigned east; Xiong followed Prince of Qi Xian in taking Hongdong and capturing Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the eastern campaign, Liu Xiong followed Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian in taking Hongdong and Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 軍還，仍與憲廻援晉州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, still with Xian he wheeled back to aid Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he turned back with Xian to relieve Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，齊後主已率大兵親自攻圍，晉州垂陷。

translations.literal: Before arriving, Qi Emperor Hou Zhu had already led a great army in person to attack and besiege; Jizhou was on the verge of falling.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Northern Qi's emperor had already come in person with a great host to besiege Jizhou, which was near collapse.

sentences.zh: 憲遣雄先往察其軍勢。

translations.literal: Xian sent Xiong ahead first to observe their army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent Liu Xiong ahead to scout the enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 雄乃率步騎千人，鳴鼓角，遙報城中。

translations.literal: Xiong then led a thousand foot and horse, sounded drums and horns, and from afar announced to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong led a thousand mixed troops, sounded drums and horns, and signaled the city from afar.

sentences.zh: 尋而高祖兵至，齊主遁走。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Gaozu's troops arrived; the Qi ruler fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Gaozu's army arrived and the Qi ruler fled.

sentences.zh: 從平幷州，拜上大將軍，進爵趙郡公，邑二千戶，舊封廻授一子。

translations.literal: Following in pacifying Bing Province, he was appointed supreme grand general, advanced to Duke of Zhao commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and his former enfeoffment was turned back and granted to one son.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Bing Province he was made supreme grand general, raised to Duke of Zhao with a fief of two thousand households, and his earlier title was transferred to a son.

sentences.zh: 明年，從平鄴城，進柱國。

translations.literal: The next year, following in pacifying Ye city, he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after the fall of Ye, he was made pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 其年，從齊王憲總北討稽胡。

translations.literal: That year, following Prince of Qi Xian in general northern campaign against the Ji Hu.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he joined Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian in the northern campaign against the Ji Hu.

sentences.zh: 軍還，出鎮幽州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he went out to garrison You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he was posted to garrison You.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年四月，突厥寇幽州，擁略居民。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, the Türks raided You Prefecture and carried off residents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuanzheng year 1 the Türks raided You and carried off the people.

sentences.zh: 雄出戰，為突厥所圍，臨陣戰歿。

translations.literal: Xiong went out to battle, was surrounded by the Türks, and died fighting on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiong rode out to fight, was surrounded by the Türks, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈亳州總管、七州諸軍事、亳州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Overall Commander of Bo Prefecture, all military affairs of seven prefectures, and Inspector of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made overall commander of Bo, commander of military affairs in seven prefectures, and inspector of Bo.

sentences.zh: 子昇嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 以雄死王事，大象末，授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Because Xiong died in service to the throne, at the end of Daxiang he was granted equal-in-protocol grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Xiong had died in the sovereign's service, Sheng was made equal-in-protocol grand general near the end of the Daxiang era.

sentences.zh: 侯植字仁幹，上谷人也。

translations.literal: Hou Zhi, styled Rengan, was a man of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhi, courtesy name Rengan, came from Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 燕散騎常侍龕之八世孫。

translations.literal: Eighth-generation descendant of Kan, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was an eighth-generation descendant of Kan, who had served Yan as regular attendant of the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 高祖恕，魏北地郡守。

translations.literal: High ancestor Shu was Northern Beidi commandery administrator of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: High ancestor Shu had served Wei as administrator of Northern Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 子孫因家于北地之三水，遂為州郡冠族。

translations.literal: His descendants established their home at Sanshui in Beidi and thus became the leading clan of the province and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The family settled at Sanshui in Beidi and became the foremost clan of the region.

sentences.zh: 父欣，

translations.literal: Father Xin,
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin was

translations.literal: (Qin) [emended: Tai]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Tai]

sentences.zh: 〔泰〕州刺史、奉義縣公。

translations.literal: 〔Tai〕 Province Inspector and Duke of Fengyi county.
translations.idiomatic: inspector of Tai Province and Duke of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 植少倜儻，有大節，容貌奇偉，武藝絕倫。

translations.literal: Zhi from youth was unconventional and bold, had great integrity, appearance extraordinarily imposing, and martial arts unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hou Zhi was free-spirited and high-minded, with a striking presence and unmatched skill in arms.

sentences.zh: 正光中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he first entered service as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Zhengguang era he began his career as an attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 尋而天下喪亂，群盜蜂起，植乃散家財，率募勇敢討賊。

translations.literal: Soon the realm fell into disorder and bandits rose everywhere; Zhi thereupon distributed his family wealth, recruited the brave, and attacked bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed into chaos and brigands swarmed the land, he spent his family fortune, gathered volunteers, and took the field against them.

sentences.zh: 以功拜統軍，遷清河郡守。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed area commander and transferred to Qinghe commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign merit won him the rank of area commander and a transfer to act as administrator of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 後從賀拔岳討万俟醜奴等，每有戰功，除義州刺史。

translations.literal: Later following He Ba Yue he attacked Wanqidu Chounu and others; whenever there was battle merit, he was appointed Yizhou provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under He Ba Yue, he fought Wanqidu Chounu and others; repeated battlefield success made him governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 在州甚有政績，為夷夏所懷。

translations.literal: In the province he had very fine administrative achievements and was cherished by barbarians and Chinese alike.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yizhou with marked success and won the trust of both tribal peoples and Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 時帝幼沖，晉公護執政，植從兄龍恩為護所親任。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was young, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held government, and Zhi's older cousin Long En was personally trusted and employed by Hu.
translations.idiomatic: While the boy emperor reigned and Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ruled the state, Hou Zhi's elder cousin Long En enjoyed Hu's personal favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 及護誅趙貴，而諸宿將等多不自安。

translations.literal: When Hu executed Zhao Gui, the various veteran generals mostly were not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu put Zhao Gui to death, many of the old commanders grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 植謂龍恩曰：「今主上春秋旣富，安危系於數公。

translations.literal: Zhi said to Long En: "Now the sovereign's years are already full; safety and peril depend on you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhi told Long En, "The emperor is grown now, and the realm's fate rests with you men at the top.

sentences.zh: 共為唇齒，尚憂不濟，況以纖介之間，自相夷滅！

translations.literal: Mutual support like lips and teeth—one still worries it may not succeed, all the more so with petty matters to destroy one another!
translations.idiomatic: Stand together like lips and teeth and you may still fail—how much worse to tear one another apart over trifles!

sentences.zh: 植恐天下之人，因此解體。

translations.literal: Zhi fears people throughout the realm will for this dissolve their unity.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the whole country will come apart because of it.

sentences.zh: 兄旣受人任使，安得知而不言。

translations.literal: Elder brother, having received a commission of trust, how can one know and not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Brother, you hold a post of trust—how can you see this and say nothing?

sentences.zh: 」龍恩竟不能用。

translations.literal: " Long En ultimately could not adopt [the advice].
translations.idiomatic: " Long En would not take his counsel.

sentences.zh: 植又乘間言於護曰：「君臣之分，情均父子，理須同其休戚，期之始終。

translations.literal: Zhi again seized an opportunity to speak to Hu, saying: "The distinction between ruler and minister—in feeling equal to father and son—reason requires sharing weal and woe through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhi later found occasion to speak to Yuwen Hu: "Between ruler and minister the bond should be as close as father and son; fortune and misfortune must be shared to the end.

sentences.zh: 明公以骨肉之親，當社稷之寄，與存與亡，在於茲日。

translations.literal: Your Excellency, as bone-and-flesh kin, bears the charge of the altars of land and grain; whether [the state] survives or perishes is decided on this day.
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's own kin and hold the fate of the realm in your hands; whether the dynasty lives or dies is decided now.

sentences.zh: 願公推誠王室，擬跡伊、周，使國有泰山之安，家傳世祿之盛，則率土之濱，莫不幸甚。

translations.literal: I hope Your Excellency will extend sincerity to the royal house, take as model the tracks of Yi and Zhou, so that the state has Mount Tai's security, the family transmits generations of emolument in splendor—then all within the bounds of the realm, none will not be exceedingly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the throne in good faith, take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as your models, and the state will stand firm as Mount Tai while your house enjoys lasting rank and wealth—then every subject under heaven will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 」護曰：「我蒙太祖厚恩，且屬當猶子，誓將以身報國，賢兄應見此心。

translations.literal: " Hu said: "I have received the Grand Progenitor's deep grace, and moreover stand as if adopted son; I swear I shall repay the state with my body—your worthy elder brother ought to see this heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu replied, "Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai showed me great favor, and I stand in his place as an adopted son; I mean to repay the state with my life—your worthy brother should know my heart.

sentences.zh: 卿今有是言，豈謂吾有他志耶。

translations.literal: You now have these words—do you mean to say I have another intention?
translations.idiomatic: Why speak to me like this—as though I harbored some other design?

sentences.zh: 」又聞其先與龍恩言，乃陰忌之。

translations.literal: " On also hearing his earlier words to Long En, he thereupon secretly bore resentment against Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Learning what Hou Zhi had said to Long En, he came to resent him in secret.

sentences.zh: 植懼不免禍，遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: Zhi feared he could not escape calamity and thereupon died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not escape punishment, Hou Zhi died of grief.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General,
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general,

translations.literal: (Zheng) [emended: Ping]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Ping]

translations.literal: 〔Ping〕
translations.idiomatic: Ping

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yang]

sentences.zh: 〔揚〕光三州諸軍事、平州刺史，諡曰節。

translations.literal: 〔Yang〕 Commander-in-Chief of the three provinces Guang and others, Ping Province Governor; posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: commander-in-chief for Ping, Yang, and Guang provinces and governor of Ping Province, with the posthumous name Jie.

sentences.zh: 子定嗣。

translations.literal: Son Ding succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ding inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 及護伏誅，龍恩與其弟大將軍、武平公萬壽竝預其禍。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, Long En and his younger brother Grand General, Duke of Wuping Wanshou both met with that calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Long En and his younger brother Wanshou, grand general and Duke of Wuping, perished in the same purge.

sentences.zh: 高祖治護事，知植忠於朝廷，乃特免其子孫。

translations.literal: Gaozu, investigating Hu's affair, knowing Zhi was loyal to the court, thereupon specially exempted his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating Yuwen Hu's crimes, Emperor Wu found that Hou Zhi had been loyal to the throne and specially spared his descendants.

sentences.zh: 定後位至車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Ding later reached Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Ding later rose to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王傑、王勇、宇文虯之徒，咸以果毅之姿，效節於擾攘之際，終能屠堅

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yuwen Qiu and the like—all with resolute and daring bearing, offered their loyalty in turbulent times—ultimately could slay the strong
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Wang Jie, Wang Yong, Yuwen Qiu, and men like them—all resolute warriors who gave their best in chaotic times—could in the end break the hardest foes

translations.literal: (Zhi) [emended: Fu]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Fu]

sentences.zh: 〔覆〕銳，立禦侮之功，裂膏壤，據勢位，固其宜也。

translations.literal: 〔Fu〕 and sharp, establish merit in repelling insult, split fertile lands, occupy powerful positions—this was indeed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: and overturn the keenest enemy lines, win glory in defense of the realm, carve out rich fiefs, and hold high command—as was only right.

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱「無求備於一人」，信矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Do not expect completeness in one man"—how true!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Do not expect every virtue in a single man"—and he was right.

sentences.zh: 夫文士懷溫恭之操，其弊也愞弱；

translations.literal: Literary men cherish gentle and respectful conduct—their defect is weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars cultivate gentleness and courtesy, yet their failing is timidity;

sentences.zh: 武夫稟剛烈之質，其失也敢悍。

translations.literal: Military men possess fierce and bold nature—their failing is reckless insolence.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers are born fierce and bold, yet their failing is rash violence.

sentences.zh: 故有使酒不遜之禍，拔劍爭功之尤。

translations.literal: Hence there are disasters of displaying arrogance when drunk, faults of drawing swords to quarrel over merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the disaster of drunken insolence and the fault of drawing swords over credit for battle.

sentences.zh: 大則莫全其生，小則僅而獲免。

translations.literal: In large matters none preserve their lives intact; in small matters they barely escape.
translations.idiomatic: At worst such men lose their lives; at best they barely survive.

sentences.zh: 耿豪、王勇，不其然乎。

translations.literal: Geng Hao, Wang Yong—is this not exactly so?
translations.idiomatic: Were not Geng Hao and Wang Yong exactly such cases?

translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
